correctness.rationale: The integer-height slice bijection counts exactly (bj+1)L_P(t-j) points per height. Summing segment linear and Pick polygon quadratic Ehrhart counts gives all displayed coefficients. For two segments the sole sign inequality and AM--GM establish the sharp volume 49. For polygon--segment joins positivity reduces precisely to two numerator signs. Pick gives universal b<=4; the primitive-edge triangle with B=41,I=0 realizes b=5 and minimal normalized volume 195. The b=7 inequalities conflict, while a 37-by-4 rectangle works at every b>=8. The standalone checker independently interpolated 3388 parameter cases from exact slice counts. A finite test is not asserted to prove the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The object is the simplest geometric join family singled out by the 2026 positivity-preservation question. The results completely characterize the first two dimensions in which sign failure can occur, quantify the absolute minimum normalized volume for three-dimensional negative joins, and determine the universal safe segment length and earliest maximum two-negative sign transition for all lattice polygons. These sharp natural boundaries are not arbitrary numerical slices; they locate the onset and complexity of positivity failure.
